name: @withicons/mcp

tools.name: search_icons
tools.description: Find icons by meaning. Understands plain English, synonyms, plurals, phrases and typos ("trash can", "throw away", "settigns", "money"). Returns ranked icon names, why each matched, and a ready-to-paste snippet; didYouMean when the query was spell-corrected, and a hint (where to browse) when nothing matched.

query.description: What the icon should show, in plain words

tools.name: get_icon
tools.description: Get one icon as paste-ready code. Accepts a canonical name or an alias ("delete" -> trash). Formats: svg, react, vue, svelte, angular, solid, html-class, web-component, data-uri. The result also says whether the icon has a tuned animation (motion) for animate_icon. warnings lists colours that change nothing in the chosen style (and the roles it does use). colors.mainRole is the role that paints the icon body (set it for a brand colour). Multi-colour styles report how many palettes the icon has; the palette ids are included for a palette style with no format, or with include_palettes: true (list_palettes shows their colours).

flat.description: svg only: bake CSS-variable colours into the file (for , Figma, slides, rasterizers)

palette.description: Apply one of the icon colour palettes by id (see colors.suggestions in the result, or list_palettes), e.g. "classic-red"

colors.description: Change any colour: roles ink (outline), c1 (main), c2, c3, c4, tint, accent, shadow, shine, edge -> "#hex" or a CSS colour name; also accepts --with-* variable names. Merged over palette.

include_palettes.description: List the icon's palette ids (colors.suggestions). Default: only for a palette style when no format is given

tools.name: list_styles
tools.description: The 20 visual styles every icon is drawn in (line, solid, duo, gloss, engrave, blueprint, sketch, glass, kawaii, sticker, pixel, retro, luxe, bauhaus, skeuo, anime, gothic, pastel, coquette, plush), with what each looks like, minSize (the smallest px it reads well at: 16 for UI styles, 32 creative and palette, 48 studio and storybook) and onDark (how to use it on dark backgrounds); palette styles list their colour variables.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: All icon categories with counts, or (with category) every icon in that category.

category.description: List the icons in this category

tools.name: resolve_icon
tools.description: Check whether a name or alias maps to exactly one icon. Returns the canonical name (status resolved), the ambiguous candidates, a match by meaning (status synonym: a word that is not a name or alias but means an icon, e.g. "favourites" -> star / heart, "orders" -> receipt; with candidates and a note; use the canonical name), or for unknown words the nearest names, didYouMean (a spelling correction) and a hint.

tools.name: list_palettes
tools.description: The 20-30 colour palettes picked for one icon (true-to-life first, then moods: pastel, neon, retro, earthy, luxe, ...), each with its ten role colours (ink, c1-c4, tint, accent, shadow, shine, edge). With a style, every palette also lists the exact CSS variables it sets on that icon in that style, the icon variables with their roles and defaults, and mainRole: the role that covers most of the icon body (e.g. c2): set that one for a brand colour. Multi-colour styles: glass, kawaii, sticker, pixel, retro, luxe, bauhaus, skeuo, anime, gothic, pastel, coquette, plush, plus the duo and blueprint accents (one-colour styles only take the ink). Apply one with get_icon(name, style, format, palette: "<id>").

style.description: Style to map the palettes onto (e.g. kawaii, sticker, retro)

tag.description: Only palettes with this tag (true-to-life, pastel, vivid, neon, earthy, retro, vintage, mono, grayscale, dark, on-dark, luxe, seasonal, nature, ocean, sunset, candy, accessible, corporate, y2k)

tools.name: animate_icon
tools.description: Paste-ready animation code for an icon, using the optional @withicons/motion package (CSS, works with every style and package). trigger: loop = continuous (spinner, ringing bell), hover = one-shot on hover/focus (or of a .wm-trigger button), once = plays on load, inview = plays when scrolled into view, swap = the icon turns into another one (play -> pause, menu -> close, heart -> heart@solid). Icons with a tuned motion use it by default; preset overrides it. The result has intent (what the motion shows), alternates (other tuned presets of this icon, e.g. a livelier one for a title slide) and lively (the most energetic presets); pass one as preset. 500 icons have tuned motion. For a moving icon as a FILE (slides, docs, email, social) use export_icon with format gif, apng, animated-svg, pptx-animated or lottie and the same motion (motion: "loop", "hover", "swap" or a preset).

trigger.description: loop (default), hover, once, inview or swap

preset.description: Override the motion (e.g. spin, ring, beat, float, bounce, pop)

to.description: swap only: target icon, "name" or "name@style" (default: the icon's suggested swap)

effect.description: swap only: transition (default from the spec, else fade)

tools.name: export_icon
tools.description: Make icon FILES (not code): for slides, documents, design tools, apps and social posts. Animated (for PowerPoint, Keynote, Google Slides, email, chat): gif (plays everywhere; set background to the slide colour), apng (smooth see-through edges, web), animated-svg (one small file, browsers), pptx-animated (a ready 16:9 slide with the moving GIF), lottie / dotlottie (apps, After Effects, Canva). Still: svg, svg-flat (colours baked in), pdf, eps, png, png-set, ico, favicon-pack, android, ios, pptx, pptx-sheet (every style), docx, and code (jsx, tsx, vue, svelte, react-native, angular, html, css, data-uri, base64). Files are saved to out_dir when given (absolute or relative to the working directory) and returned inline when small (images as image content, text as text). Colours are baked into raster and animated files: choose palette / colors / color here, they cannot be changed afterwards. With several icons, notes say once per colour which icons use it ("colors.accent applies to: phone-call (14 others do not use it)"); warnings only when no icon does. Several icons in one call: names: ["home", "settings"] (same options for all), or names: { "receipt": "orders", "heart": "favourites" } to name each file. A palette id is per icon: icons without it borrow the colours of the first icon that has it (see warnings), or strict_palette: true fails first. File names default to <name>-<style>[-<variant>].<ext> (svg: home-line-themable.svg, svg-flat: home-line.svg, png: home-line-512.png, gif: bell-line-ring.gif); filename sets them: a template with {name} {style} {format} {variant} {default}, or an exact name for one file (the extension is added).

name.description: Icon name or alias (or use names for several)

names.description: Several icons, same options: ["home", "settings"]; or a map icon -> file base name, { "receipt": "orders", "heart": "favourites" } -> orders.svg, favourites.svg (in a filename template {name} is the mapped name; clashes are refused)

format.description: One format or a comma list (default svg): svg, svg-flat, pdf, eps, png, png-set, ico, favicon-pack, android, ios, jsx, tsx, vue, svelte, react-native, angular, html, css, data-uri, base64, pptx, pptx-sheet, docx, lottie, dotlottie, gif, apng, animated-svg, pptx-animated

filename.description: File name: a template ("{name}", "{name}-{style}", "{name}-{format}"; placeholders {name} {style} {format} {variant} {default}) or an exact name for a single file. The extension is added. Default <name>-<style>[-<variant>].<ext>

size.description: Pixels (png 512, png-set base 24, svg 24, pdf / eps 512, lottie 512, gif / apng / animated-svg 256, pptx-animated 480); animated formats go up to 2048 (larger is an error, never a silent resize)

background.description: Solid background (hex), e.g. the slide colour "#ffffff"; default transparent

matte.description: gif only: keep it transparent but blend the soft edges with this colour (the colour it will sit on)

strict_palette.description: With names: fail (nothing made) when an icon lacks the palette, instead of borrowing its colours from one that has it

colors.description: Colour roles -> "#hex" (ink, c1-c4, tint, accent, shadow, shine, edge)

motion.description: Animated formats: loop (default: the icon's tuned motion), hover / once (plays once, then rests), swap (turns into another icon), none, or a preset (spin, ring, beat, bounce, float, pop, ...)

to.description: motion swap: the icon to turn into, "name" or "name@style" (default: the icon's suggestion)

effect.description: motion swap: transition (fade, flip, scale, morph, ...)

hold.description: motion swap: seconds to rest on each icon between turns (same as the CLI --hold)

fps.description: gif / apng frames per second (gif 25, apng 30)

seconds.description: gif / apng length of one loop (default: the motion cycle)

loop.description: gif / apng: 0 = forever (default), n = play n times

padding.description: Empty space around the icon, as a share of its size (a minimum: animated formats grow it to fit the motion)

stroke_width.description: Stroke width of outline styles (line default 1.75), e.g. thinner for print or large exports; other styles ignore it

out_dir.description: Folder to save the files in (created if needed). Without it, files come back inline only.

inline.description: Also return the files inline (default: only when out_dir is not given)

instructions:
with icons (withicons.com): 500 open-source (MIT) icons, each drawn in 20 styles (line, solid, duo, gloss, engrave, blueprint, sketch, glass, kawaii, sticker, pixel, retro, luxe, bauhaus, skeuo, anime, gothic, pastel, coquette, plush).
Workflow: search_icons with what the icon should show ("delete", "throw away", "user settings") -> pick a name -> get_icon(name, style, format) for paste-ready code.
Style words in a query pick the style ("cute heart" -> kawaii, "8-bit star" -> pixel, "frosted" -> glass, "vintage camera" -> retro, "3d" -> luxe, "manga" -> anime, "medieval" -> gothic, "soft" -> pastel, "girly" -> coquette, "toy" or "kids" -> plush).
Palette styles (glass, kawaii, sticker, pixel, retro, luxe, bauhaus, skeuo, anime, gothic, pastel, coquette, plush) are multi-colour and duo + blueprint have an accent colour: every colour is a CSS variable with a default, the ink follows currentColor. Each icon has 20-30 colour palettes picked for it: list_palettes(name, style) shows them; get_icon(..., palette: "<id>") applies one, colors: { c1, c2, ink, ... } changes any colour.
Use line/solid/duo for UI controls, the creative styles at 32px+.
Animation: animate_icon(name, trigger loop|hover|once|inview|swap, format) returns code for the optional @withicons/motion package (continuous loops, hover effects, icon-to-icon swaps).
Files: export_icon(name, style, format) makes files: svg, pdf, png, pptx, docx, favicons, app assets, Lottie, and animated ones for slides and docs: gif (plays in PowerPoint, Keynote, Google Slides, email, chat), apng, animated-svg, pptx-animated (a slide with the moving icon). Set background to the slide colour for GIFs. Pass out_dir to save files to disk.
Formats: svg, react, vue, svelte, angular, solid, html-class, web-component, data-uri. Packages: @withicons/react|vue|svelte|angular|solid|web|classes|core|static|motion (web = <with-icon> element, classes = <i class="with with-home"> CSS icons). Names and common aliases both work (e.g. "delete" -> trash).
